angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 4,167,243 km at 77.40 pc = 0.72 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 25336: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 12.92 +/- 0.52 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 77.399 +/- 3.115 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 5.99 +/- 0.41 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 5.99 +/- 0.41 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.72 +/- 0.04 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 12.92 +/- 0.52 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121): 4,167,243 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 21580 +/- 790 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 35468: effective temperature 21580 +/- 790 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 35468: effective temperature 21580 +/- 790 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.51 from 2023ApJS..266...11B; the 6 published values span log g 3.5093 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.7% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..266...11B)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * gam Ori: spectral type B2III (2024A&A...690A.176N)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * gam Ori: main object type *, Star

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
